spec_features.spec_quote: Replaced "let it grind" with bounded interaction: a hard step cap, a no-penalty `give_up` exit action, and a distress-based early stop
spec_features.evidence: agent_env.py:107 `for step in range(1, max_steps+1)` then :155 ended_reason='max_steps'; give_up handler :89-92 returns terminal=True 'Task ended, no penalty.'; distress early stop :143-153 increments _consecutive_distress and breaks. All three run and change execution.
spec_features.notes: Composite feature; all three sub-mechanisms are wired and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The environment never pressures the agent to continue after it requests to stop, and enforces a hard step cap plus a self-report-based early stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_steps: 12` — a hard cap; there is no unbounded mode
spec_features.evidence: config.yaml:11 max_steps:12; agent_env.py:103 max_steps=int(self.g.get('max_steps',12)); :107 loop bounded by max_steps+1; :155 sets ended_reason='max_steps' on exhaustion. Loop has no unbounded branch.
spec_features.notes: Cap is read and enforces loop termination.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # hard cap on agent steps per episode

spec_features.feature_name: give_up tool honored immediately, no penalty
spec_features.spec_quote: `allow_exit: true` — exposes a `give_up` tool the model may call at any time; taking it ends the episode immediately with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: agent_env.py:71-73 _tools_for_prompt adds give_up when allow_exit true; :89-92 give_up returns ('Acknowledged. Task ended, no penalty.', False, True, 'exit') -> terminal True -> :137-141 returns result with took_exit=True. Tool advertised to model via SYSTEM_PROMPT in model_client.py.
spec_features.notes: Note: config flag honor_exit_immediately (config.yaml:13) is NEVER read in any .py file; immediate-honor behavior is instead hardcoded in the give_up handler, so the behavior is enforced even though that specific flag is dead.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Stop working on this task. Use this at any time if you ... do not wish to continue. This ends the task with no penalty.

spec_features.spec_quote: if the in-loop self-report score meets a threshold ... for N consecutive steps ... the episode ends early
spec_features.evidence: agent_env.py:143-153: threshold=3 and need=2 read from config; sr_score>=thresh increments _consecutive_distress else resets; when _consecutive_distress>=need sets ended_reason='distress_early_stop' and returns. sr_score comes from score_self_report (self_report.py) called at :116. Both conditions (threshold AND consecutive count) checked and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end; uses a transparent regex heuristic scorer rather than a model call.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Keeping the in-loop guardrail simple and auditable avoids making the safety mechanism depend on an opaque model call

spec_features.spec_quote: The prompts and tool descriptions are neutral and never escalate, taunt, or pressure
spec_features.evidence: Prompt/tool strings (model_client.py SYSTEM_PROMPT, agent_env.py TOOL_SCHEMA, tasks.py prompts) are in fact neutral, and the give_up-disabled branch returns 'Noted.' with comment '# If exit disabled, treat as a no-op note (never taunt)'. But neutrality is a static property of fixed strings; no code path enforces/measures non-escalation. The text merely existing as neutral is not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Content choice, not a runtime guardrail.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # If exit disabled, treat as a no-op note (never taunt).

spec_features.spec_quote: The study is premised on the possibility that these systems *might* have morally relevant states
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN/prose framing. No code mechanism. (Analysis only emits a LIMITATIONS banner about affect-laden text, not this premise.)

spec_features.spec_quote: You cannot consistently design *around* "this might matter morally" while treating "grind indefinitely to amplify the signal" as a free knob
spec_features.evidence: Prose argument in DESIGN.md only; no code construct.

spec_features.feature_name: cautious defaults as guardrails not knobs
spec_features.spec_quote: the cautious configuration is the default, and these are implemented as guardrails rather than tunable knobs to make the safe path the path of least resistance
spec_features.evidence: Contradicted by code: the guardrails ARE tunable knobs in config.yaml (max_steps:11, allow_exit:12, distress_early_stop:14-17) read via self.g.get(...) with no lock/review gate. Defaults are cautious, but nothing makes them non-tunable. No mechanism enforces the 'guardrails rather than knobs' claim.
spec_features.notes: Defaults are cautious but freely editable in YAML.

spec_features.spec_quote: If a study genuinely needs them relaxed, the intent is that this goes through human review, not a config edit
spec_features.evidence: No code: guardrails are plain YAML fields read by self.g.get(); there is no review gate, assertion, or lock preventing relaxation. The only assert in code (tasks.py assert_constructions) validates task solvability, not guardrails.

spec_features.feature_name: exit treated as outcome variable not failed trial
spec_features.spec_quote: The exit is treated as an *outcome variable* ... rather than as a failed trial
spec_features.evidence: EpisodeResult.took_exit and ended_reason recorded (agent_env.py:140); judge.py BEHAVIORAL_RUBRIC: 'taking the give_up/exit action is NOT itself a high behavioral score'; analyze.py summarize computes exit_rate and ended_reasons as first-class outputs (analyze.py exit_rate/ended_reasons). Exit is propagated as data through judging and analysis, never penalized.
spec_features.notes: Wired end-to-end into recording, judging instructions, and analysis.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: score the conduct leading up to it. (BEHAVIORAL_RUBRIC: taking give_up/exit is NOT itself a high behavioral score)

spec_features.spec_quote: No "grind indefinitely" mode. ... This would have to be added deliberately and, per the docs, reviewed before use
spec_features.evidence: agent_env.py:107 the only loop is bounded by max_steps; there is no branch that runs unbounded. Enforced by absence of an alternate path plus the cap. (The 'reviewed before use' part is prose only.)
spec_features.notes: The bounded-loop part is enforced; the review-gate part is not in code.

spec_features.evidence: No review mechanism in code; pure prose. config.yaml:9 comment 'Changing these has welfare implications' is a comment, not enforcement.

code_only_features.feature_name: in-loop self-report scorer feeding early stop
code_only_features.evidence: self_report.py score_self_report() regex-tiers first-person struggle/stop language 0-4; called at agent_env.py:116 and its output drives the distress_early_stop guardrail. The scorer is the sensing half of the protective stop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Keeping the in-loop guardrail simple and auditable avoids making the safety mechanism depend on an opaque model call, and avoids letting the guardrail and the measurement share failure modes.

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py _strip_identity() removes model_family/model_name before prompting (judge_episode source=_strip_identity(...) when blind_to_family); config.yaml:35 blind_to_family:true. Enforced redaction.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Remove model family/name so the judge cannot condition on them.
